abstract.para: This section describes how to configure the guest virtual machine so that it can use the host's &nvidia; GPU. Use virt-manager or virt-install to install the guest VM. Find more details in Guest installation.

section.title: Requirements for the guest configuration
section.para: During the guest VM installation, select Customize configuration before install and configure the following devices:

listitem.para: Use Q35 chipset for proper PCIe passthrough with modern GPUs.
Install the guest VM using UEFI firmware.
Find more information in Configuring Virtual Machines with &vmm;.
Add the host PCI device (for example, 03:00.0) to the guest. Find more information in Assigning Host Devices to Virtual Machines.
For the best performance, we recommend using virtio drivers for the network card and storage.

step.para: Download the driver RPM package from the official &nvidia; driver download page at .

note.title: Minimum driver version for &cuda;
note.para: &cuda; 13.3 requires driver version 610.43.02 or newer. The minimum driver version for &cuda; 13.x is 580.

step.para: Because the installer needs to compile the &nvidia; driver modules, install the gcc-c++ and kernel-devel packages.

&nvidia; driver modules are unsigned, so disable Secure Boot on the guest. Either disable it in the UEFI firmware setup, or use mokutil to enroll a Machine Owner Key. Find more information about &uefisecboot; in Using &uefisecboot;.

note.title: Display issues
note.para: After you have installed the &nvidia; drivers, the virt-manager display loses its connection to the guest OS. To access the guest VM, you must either login via ssh, change to the console interface, or install a dedicated VNC server in the guest. note.title: &mswin; driver no longer bundled with the &cuda; Toolkit
note.para: Starting with &cuda; 13.1, the &mswin; display driver is no longer bundled with the &cuda; Toolkit. You must download and install the appropriate &nvidia; driver separately from the official &nvidia; driver download page.
